paragraphs.title: Praise and Deliverance Through Turning to God

easy.explanation: David says, “I will bless the LORD at all times.”
easy.q: What does David say he will do at all times?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the humble shall hear thereof, and be glad.”
easy.q: Who will hear David’s praise and be glad?

answers: He heard and delivered him from his fears
medium.explanation: The LORD heard David and delivered him from all his fears.
medium.q: What did the LORD do for David when he sought Him?

medium.explanation: David calls others to praise and exalt the LORD together.
medium.q: What does “magnify the LORD” mean in this passage?

answers: The LORD hears and saves him from his troubles
medium.explanation: The verse says the LORD heard him and saved him out of all his troubles.
medium.q: What happens to the poor man who cries to the LORD?

answers: His deliverance becomes a reason for shared praise
He wants to praise God alone
He no longer trusts the LORD
challenge.explanation: David invites others to join him in exalting the LORD.
challenge.q: What does David’s invitation to magnify the LORD together show?

answers: Personal praise leads to shared praise and testimony of deliverance
Fear leads to silence and despair
Strength leads to dependence on human power
challenge.explanation: David begins with personal praise, invites others to join, and describes God’s deliverance.
challenge.q: What progression appears in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The angel encamps around those who fear the LORD and delivers them.
challenge.q: Who is surrounded and delivered by the angel of the LORD?

short_answers.question: According to verse 4, from what did the LORD deliver David?
short_answers.explanation: David says, “he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.”

short_answers.question: What are the humble invited to do according to verse 3?
short_answers.answer: Join in magnifying and exalting the LORD.
short_answers.explanation: David says, “O magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt his name together.”

short_answers.question: What does the angel of the LORD do for those who fear Him?
short_answers.answer: He encamps around them and delivers them.
short_answers.explanation: The angel protects and delivers those who fear the LORD.

paragraphs.title: Experiencing God’s Goodness and Care for His Devotees

answers: That the young lions are hungry
easy.explanation: The verse says, “O taste and see that the LORD is good.”
easy.q: What are the readers invited to taste and see?

answers: The man who trusts in the LORD
The man who trusts in his strength
easy.explanation: The man who trusts in the LORD is called blessed.
The verse says those who seek the LORD shall not want any good thing.
easy.q: Who shall not want any good thing?

answers: By trusting and taking refuge in Him
By relying only on human strength
medium.explanation: The passage connects experiencing God’s goodness with trusting Him.
medium.q: How can a person experience the LORD’s goodness according to these verses?

answers: Young lions may lack and hunger, but those who seek the LORD shall not want any good thing
Young lions are satisfied, but those who seek the LORD suffer
Young lions seek the LORD, but His people flee
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts hungry young lions with the provision promised to those who seek the LORD.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the young lions and those who seek the LORD?

answers: To reverence and faithfully serve Him
medium.explanation: The passage uses fear of the LORD to describe devoted reverence toward Him.
medium.q: What does “fear the LORD” mean in this context?

answers: Natural strength alone does not guarantee provision; the LORD is the source of good
The strongest people never lack anything
Faith has no connection to a person’s needs
challenge.explanation: Even powerful young lions may hunger, while those who seek the LORD are promised good.
challenge.q: What does the image of hungry young lions suggest about true security?

answers: Experiencing God’s goodness is connected with trusting Him
Experiencing God’s goodness removes the need for trust
challenge.explanation: The invitation to experience God’s goodness is joined to the blessing of trusting Him.
challenge.q: How are “taste and see” and “blessed is the man that trusteth in him” related?

answers: The LORD is good and cares for those who reverence and seek Him
Human strength is the believer’s protection
The young lions provide for God’s people
challenge.explanation: The verses emphasize God’s goodness and care for those who fear and seek Him.
challenge.q: What central idea unites these verses?

paragraphs.title: Guidance for a Good Life and Peace

easy.explanation: David says, “Come, ye children, hearken unto me.”
easy.q: Whom does David invite to listen to him?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Keep thy tongue from evil.”
easy.q: What should a person keep from evil?

easy.explanation: The instruction is to “seek peace, and pursue it.”
easy.q: What should a person seek and pursue?

answers: Fear the LORD, guard speech, depart from evil, do good, and pursue peace
Speak guile, do evil, and seek conflict
Remain silent and avoid every action
medium.explanation: David teaches reverence, truthful speech, good conduct, and active pursuit of peace.
medium.q: What sequence of instruction appears in these verses?

medium.explanation: Guile means deceptive or dishonest speech.

answers: Guarding speech is part of fearing God and doing what is good
Speech does not matter if actions are good
Guarding speech replaces the need to pursue peace
medium.explanation: David includes truthful speech among the instructions for seeing good and living rightly.
medium.q: How is speech connected with a good life?

answers: Peace requires active effort rather than passive waiting
challenge.explanation: The word “pursue” shows that peace must be actively sought.
challenge.q: What does the command to “pursue” peace show?

answers: A person must guard speech while also turning from evil and doing good
Good actions matter only when speech is evil
challenge.explanation: The passage joins control of speech with righteous actions.
challenge.q: What relationship between speech and conduct appears in David’s instruction?

answers: Fearing the LORD, speaking truthfully, rejecting evil, doing good, and pursuing peace
Avoiding every action and remaining silent
challenge.explanation: These instructions form David’s practical path toward a good life.
challenge.q: According to these verses, what is the path to seeing good?

paragraphs.title: God’s Watchfulness Over the Righteous and the Suffering

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The eyes of the LORD are upon the righteous.”
easy.q: Upon whom are the eyes of the LORD?

easy.explanation: The LORD is near to those who are of a broken heart.
easy.q: To whom is the LORD near?

easy.explanation: The passage says the LORD delivers the righteous out of all their troubles.
easy.q: From what does the LORD deliver the righteous?

answers: He sends them to the wicked
medium.explanation: The verse says, “The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth.”
medium.q: What does the LORD do when the righteous cry?

medium.explanation: A contrite spirit is humbled and repentant.

answers: The righteous may have many troubles, but the LORD delivers him from them all
Trouble proves that the LORD does not hear
medium.explanation: The verse acknowledges many afflictions while affirming God’s complete deliverance.
medium.q: What relationship is shown between the righteous person’s troubles and deliverance?

answers: God’s care does not mean the absence of trouble, but includes hearing, nearness, and deliverance
God cares only when there is no trouble
Suffering proves that the righteous have no relationship with God
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions affliction while emphasizing God’s attentive and saving presence.
challenge.q: How do these verses present God’s care alongside the suffering of the righteous?

answers: The LORD preserves and protects the righteous
challenge.explanation: The verse uses the preservation of the bones to describe God’s protection.
challenge.q: What does “He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken” communicate?

answers: He hears their cry, is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the contrite
He hides His face and abandons them
He sends them to do evil
challenge.explanation: These actions summarize the LORD’s compassionate response in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the LORD’s response to the suffering?

paragraphs.title: The Fate of the Wicked and the Protection of Those Who Trust God

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Evil shall slay the wicked.”
easy.q: What will evil do to the wicked?

answers: They shall be protected from all consequences
easy.explanation: The verse says those who hate the righteous shall be desolate.
easy.q: What will happen to those who hate the righteous?

answers: The soul of those who do evil
The soul of the young lions
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD redeemeth the soul of his servants.”
easy.q: Whose soul does the LORD redeem?

answers: The wicked are slain and become desolate, while those who trust in the LORD are redeemed and protected
The wicked are redeemed, while those who trust in the LORD are punished
Both groups are described as needing no help
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts the destruction of the wicked with the redemption of those who trust in God.
medium.q: What contrast appears between the wicked and those who trust in the LORD?

medium.explanation: Desolate means abandoned, ruined, or left without help.
medium.q: What does “desolate” mean in this passage?

answers: Those who trust in the LORD
medium.explanation: The verse says none of those who trust in Him shall be desolate.
medium.q: Who will not be desolate according to the final line?

answers: Evil itself brings about the wicked person’s destruction
The righteous directly destroy every wicked person
Peace causes the wicked person’s death
challenge.explanation: The verse presents evil itself as leading to the wicked person’s destruction.
challenge.q: What does “Evil shall slay the wicked” suggest about the source of the wicked person’s ruin?

answers: Destruction and desolation for the wicked versus redemption and security for those who trust the LORD
Hunger for young lions versus abundance for the wicked
challenge.explanation: The verses contrast the fate of the wicked with the protection of God’s servants.
challenge.q: What major contrast is expressed in these two verses?

answers: Those who trust Him are redeemed and not abandoned, while evil brings ruin to the wicked
Trusting the LORD does not affect a person’s fate
Only those who do evil receive redemption
challenge.explanation: The ending affirms God’s redemption and protection of those who trust Him.
challenge.q: How do these verses conclude the psalm’s message about trusting the LORD?
